# FieldRoutes API — Community Reference

A curated, corrected FieldRoutes OpenAPI spec — more complete than the vendor's
published docs (it documents ~90 endpoints and many fields FieldRoutes omits),
corrected for known documentation errors, and auto-synced from
[fieldroutes.dev](https://fieldroutes.dev) every week.

This is an **unofficial** reference maintained independently of FieldRoutes.
For account-specific or support issues, contact **apisupport@fieldroutes.com**.

**Spot an error, a stale field, or a missing endpoint?**
[Open an issue](https://github.com/alecbolingbroke/docs/issues) —
corrections are welcome and get folded into the next sync.

## Getting started

Every call is a POST (or GET) to `https://YOURDOMAIN.pestroutes.com/api/{entity}/{action}`
with `authenticationKey` + `authenticationToken` (and usually `officeID`).

```
POST https://YOURDOMAIN.pestroutes.com/api/customer/search
Content-Type: application/json

{ "authenticationKey": "…", "authenticationToken": "…",
  "lname": "Doe", "includeData": 1 }
```

You can also pull the vendor's own raw spec at any time:
`/api/documentation/swagger?authenticationKey=xxx&authenticationToken=xxx`.

## Limits you need to design around

| Limit | Value | What to do about it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/search` result set | **50,000 IDs** | Exactly 50,000 back means there are more. Page on the primary key with `>` and the last ID of the previous page until a set returns short. |
| `/get` entities | **1,000** | Chunk your ID lists. Inputs past the limit may be silently truncated — send `authenticationKey`/`authenticationToken` **last** so a truncated request fails outright instead of half-executing. |
| `includeData=1` on search | **1,000 resolved** | Overflow IDs come back in `{entity}IDsNoDataExported`; fetch those separately. |
| `bulkEntities` per write | **100** | Split larger batches and stagger them. |
| Rate | **3,000 reads + 3,000 writes per office, 60/min** | Default cap. See the FAQ on pacing before you go near it. |

## Keys and office scope

- By default a key is bound to **one office**: reads get an implied `officeIDs`
  filter and writes an implied `officeID`.
- **Global keys** may pass any `officeIDs` filter on search and any `officeID` on
  writes (`officeIDs: 0` = all offices).
- **Key grouping:** each key has its own read/write limits by default. Keys can be
  grouped on request so their limits and usage aggregate into a shared pool.

## Core entities
- **Office** — a branch/market. Almost everything is scoped by `officeID`.
- **Customer** — the account holder / serviced property (`customerID`); the hub other records hang off.
- **Subscription** — a customer's recurring service plan (recurring revenue): service type, billing frequency, charges/addons.
- **Appointment** — a single scheduled visit. Key fields: `date`, `status`, `assignedTech`, `spotID`, `routeID`, `cancellationReasonID`.
- **Route** — a tech's day of stops for one `date`; carries `groupID`/`groupTitle` and `assignedTech` (`0` = unassigned). The service date lives here, not on the group.
- **Spot** — a bookable time slot on a route (`start`/`end`, `spotCapacity`). `currentAppointment` empty = open; `blockReason` set = blocked. `/spot/reserve` holds one for `duration` minutes (a lock, not a booking).
- **Group** — a routing template/team that routes are scheduled onto. Thin entity (`groupID`, `templateID`, `dateUpdated`); has no service date.
- **Ticket** — an invoice / charge document.
- **Note** — a comment on a customer/appointment; `contactType` sets the kind.

## Flags & reasons
- **Generic Flag** (`genericFlagAssignment`) — a tag attached to an entity (CUST/APPT). The flag set is defined per-office, so it's the usual place custom attributes end up (property characteristics, reason codes, campaign tags).
- **customerFlag** — flags on the customer record (e.g. `pendingCancel`).
- **contactType** — the note type, configured per-office under **Admin > Preferences > Notes**. The IDs are *not* portable between offices or tenants — look yours up rather than hardcoding a number you saw in someone else's integration.
- **cancellationReason** — coded reasons an appointment was cancelled/no-showed (`cancellationReasonID`).

## Try it from this page

The **Try it** tab runs real calls against your own tenant. Enter your host
(`mycompany.fieldroutes.com`), key and token in the bar at the top, then pick an
endpoint and hit *Execute*. Requests go **straight from your browser to your
FieldRoutes host** — this site has no backend and never sees your credentials.

Writes are blocked until you explicitly tick **Allow write operations**, because
`create`/`update`/`delete` hit live data with no undo.

## Status & scheduling
- **Appointment status** (integer): `-1` = Cancelled · `-2` = Re-Scheduled · `0` = Pending · `1` = Completed · `2` = No Show.
  `-2` is easy to miss and matters for reporting: an appointment that was no-showed
  and then rescheduled **no longer carries status `2`**, so a no-show report filtered
  on `2` alone undercounts. A reschedule also populates `rescheduleReasonID` — a
  different lookup from `cancellationReasonID`.
- **assignedTech** — employee on a route/appointment; `0` = none.
- **apiCanSchedule** — send `1` on route/spot search to return only the slots the API may schedule onto — the gate for programmatic scheduling.

## API conventions

**`/search` → `/get`.** `/{entity}/search` returns IDs; feed them to `/{entity}/get`
for the full records. `includeData=1` short-circuits that for the first 1,000.

**Every search parameter** takes either a plain value or a query object:

```json
{ "dateUpdated": { "operator": ">", "value": "2026-01-01 00:00:00" } }
```

| Operator type | Accepted values |
| --- | --- |
| Comparison | `=` `!=` `>` `<` `>=` `<=` |
| Set / range | `IN` `BETWEEN` |
| Text | `LIKE` `STARTSWITH` `ENDSWITH` `CONTAINS` |

**Auth** — every call needs `authenticationKey` + `authenticationToken`, and usually
`officeID`. **accessControl** profiles (the view/edit/financial flags on an employee)
gate what a key is allowed to do.

## Silent failures you have to design around

The API's most expensive failure mode is not an error — it's a `200` that did
nothing. Each of these has been observed in production.

**A read can return `200` + `success: true` + an empty array for a record that
exists.** There is no `429`, no `errorMessage`, and nothing to distinguish it from a
genuine not-found. Failures arrive in bursts, which suggests a server-side window
rather than per-record state — the same call for the same ID succeeds minutes later.

> Treat an empty read as **retryable, not as "deleted"**. Retry with exponential
> backoff and jitter, bounded by a budget that stays under your own function's
> timeout. Code that does `if (!rows.length) throw new Error('not found')` will
> silently drop real records.

**A write can return `200` with `success: false` in the body.** Check `success` on
every mutating call; the HTTP status alone will not tell you the write landed.

**A write can also report success while ignoring part of your payload.** Look for
**`ignoredParams`** in the response — a parameter the endpoint does not accept is
dropped there rather than rejected. Notably, `/appointment/update` accepts
`cancelledBy` but ignores `cancellationReasonID`; the latter is cleared by the
platform when an appointment leaves No Show status and cannot be written back
through any update endpoint. If you need that reason to survive a status change,
persist it yourself before the transition, or read it from a flag instead.

**Read your writes back when it matters.** For flag assignments in particular, a
`200` is not proof the assignment is visible. Make the read-back advisory — alert on
a mismatch rather than aborting, or a false negative will abort work that actually
succeeded.

### Singular vs plural parameter names are load-bearing

Several endpoints accept a plural filter and **silently ignore the singular form**,
which fails in the worst possible direction — not an error, not an empty set, but a
wrong result set that looks plausible:

| Endpoint | Correct | What the singular does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/genericFlagAssignment/search` | `entityIDs` | `entityID` is ignored — returns **every assignment in the system** |
| `/appointment/search` | `customerIDs` | `customerID` lands in `ignoredParams` — returns **every appointment** (capped at 50,000) |
| `/appointment/search` | `officeIDs` | singular `officeID` returns `count: 0` |

**`/genericFlagAssignment/*` search and get need `officeIDs: 0` and must not receive
a singular `officeID` at all.** Sending `officeID` alone returns `count: 0`, and
sending **both** `officeID` and `officeIDs: 0` also returns `count: 0`. If you have a
shared request helper that injects `officeID` on every call, it needs an escape hatch
for these endpoints.

**`/appointment/search` defaults to `status IN (0,1)`.** No Show, Re-Scheduled and Cancelled
are excluded unless you pass `status` explicitly, so any report built on an unfiltered
appointment search undercounts silently.

### Credentials come back in every response

Responses echo the `authenticationKey` and `authenticationToken` you sent inside a
`params` object, and most HTTP clients attach the outbound request body to their
error objects too. **So `console.error(err)` or logging `err.response.data` writes
live credentials into your logs**, where they persist for the retention window.

> Log the status and `errorMessage`, never the whole body — and if you find you have
> been logging it, rotating the key is the remediation, not just fixing the log line.

### Trigger-rule webhooks

If you drive integrations from FieldRoutes' trigger rules rather than by polling:

- **They post `multipart/form-data`, not JSON.** Serverless platforms commonly leave
  multipart bodies unparsed, so a handler written for JSON sees an unparsed buffer and
  reports fields "missing" when every field was present.
- **A failed delivery is not retried.** There is no redelivery and no dead-letter
  queue, so if your handler drops the request the event is gone. Return `200` and
  handle failures internally, or accept that non-2xx means the event is lost.
- **They fire on a status *transition*.** Applying a flag or setting a field without
  moving the status will not fire a rule that watches that transition — which is why
  a record can look correctly tagged in the UI while no notification ever went out.

## Building tools against this spec

The published spec carries extra metadata to make code generation and agent tooling
straightforward — it's the intended backbone for an MCP server or SDK:

- **`tags`** — every operation is tagged with its entity (`customer`, `spot`, …), and
  `x-tagGroups` sorts those 62 entities into six sections. Natural tool namespaces.
- **`x-fr-write: true`** — set on every mutating operation. Use it to gate writes
  behind confirmation, or to expose a read-only tool surface by default.
- **Machine-readable artifacts** — `fieldroutes-swagger-docs.json` (canonical) and
  `fieldroutes-swagger-docs.with-summaries.json` (adds human-readable operation
  titles). Both are regenerated by the same weekly pipeline as this page.

Note that `produces` is corrected to `application/json` here. FieldRoutes declares
`text/html`, but the API is content-negotiated and answers a request for text/html
with a **406** — a client that honours the vendor's declared type gets rejected.

## Common workflows

Examples below use the vendor's `apiModule` JS helper (from
[fieldroutes.dev/examples](https://fieldroutes.dev/examples), which has the full
runnable set); the same shapes apply to any HTTP client.

**Incremental sync — pull everything changed since your last run**

```js
apiModule.search('customer', {
  dateUpdated: { operator: '>', value: '2022-03-01 00:00:00' },
  includeData: 1
}, /* fullResult */ 1).then(console.log);
```

**Global lookup by phone (global key)**

```js
apiModule.search('customer', { officeIDs: 0, phone: '5558675309', includeData: 1 });
```

**Create a customer with a subscription**

```js
apiModule.call('customer', 'create', { fname: 'John', lname: 'Doe' })
  .then(r => apiModule.call('subscription', 'create', {
    customerID: r.result,
    serviceID: 1,
    active: 1,
    initialCharge: 200,      // charged on the initial service
    serviceCharge: 100,      // charged per recurring service
    agreementLength: 12,     // months
    preferredDays: 4,        // 0=SUN … 6=SAT
    preferredStart: '09:00:00',
    preferredEnd: '17:00:00',
    preferredTech: 1         // employeeID; 0 = no preference
  }));
```

**Turn a subscription into a lead** — create it, then set the lead stage via
`subscription/updateLeadStage` (`stageID` + `status`).

**Addons** — both `initialAddons` and recurring `addons` take
`{ description, quantity, amount, productID, serviceID, taxable, creditTo, unitID }`.
A negative `amount` is a discount.

**Payment profiles** — `paymentProfile/create` with `paymentMethod` `1` = credit
card, `2` = ACH, plus `gateway` (`payrix`, `authorize`, `nmi`, `brain`, `element`).
Card profiles take `merchantID`/`merchantToken` from the gateway's tokenizer; ACH
takes `accountNumber`/`routingNumber`. **Confirm the active gateway with the office
admin first** — profiles created against an inactive gateway may be unusable.
Refunds are `payment/createRefund` with `paymentID` + `amount`.

**Bulk write (≤100 per request)**

```js
apiModule.call('customer', 'create', {
  officeID: 1,
  bulkEntities: [{ fname: 'A', lname: 'One' }, { fname: 'B', lname: 'Two' }]
});
```

For large update sets driven off a search or CSV, stagger the writes
(`apiModule.staggeredWrite(entity, action, rows, concurrency)`) rather than firing
them all at once.

**Documents & contracts** — `document/createEncoded` (`encodedFile`) and
`contract/create` (`base64EncodedFile`) take base64 with the data-URL prefix
stripped.

**dataLink** — attach arbitrary JSON to a record (`dataLink` on create/update, or
the `dataLink` entity). Pass `dataLink: 1` on search/get to have it resolved back.

**Find the best spot for an address**

```js
apiModule.search('route', {
  date: { operator: 'between', value: ['2020-09-24', '2020-09-30'] },
  latitude: lat, longitude: lng, apiCanSchedule: 1, includeData: 1
})
// sort routes by averageDistance, take the closest few, then:
.then(routeIDs => apiModule.search('spot', {
  routeIDs, date: dateFilter, latitude: lat, longitude: lng,
  apiCanSchedule: 1, ignoreInitialDriveTime: 1, includeData: 1
}));
```

Spots come back ordered by distance from the tech's previous stop, so the first
`open` spot is usually the right one. If the appointment `duration` exceeds
`spotCapacity`, walk `nextSpotID` until the full duration is covered.
`ignoreInitialDriveTime: 1` stops the tech's start/end location from being weighed
once a route already has an appointment on it.

**Hiding keys from the browser** — don't ship `authenticationKey`/`Token` to a
front end. Proxy through your own middleware and inject the credentials
server-side.

## FAQ

**Can we increase our API limits?**
Premium API limits are capped by default at **3,000 reads and 3,000 writes per
office, at 60/minute**. If your needs exceed that, email
**apisupport@fieldroutes.com** for a consultation.

**Something went wrong — are there request logs?**
Yes. Reach out to **apisupport@fieldroutes.com** and they can pull them.

**How should I pace my requests?**
Throttle deliberately and treat the per-office limits as a shared budget, not a
target. A few practical rules that hold up well in production:

- **Never spike the API.** Bursting through a large ID list at full speed will
  exhaust an office's read or write budget and degrade every other integration
  (and the FieldRoutes UI) pointed at that office.
- **Cap concurrency**, don't fan out. Staggered writes with a small concurrency
  (≈4–8 in flight) are the norm; `apiModule.staggeredWrite` does this for you.
- **Stay well under 60/minute per office**, and remember limits are *per office*
  unless your keys have been grouped into a shared pool — in which case every
  integration on those keys is drawing from the same budget.
- **Batch instead of looping.** Use `/search` + `includeData=1`, `/get` with up to
  1,000 IDs, and `bulkEntities` (≤100) rather than one call per record.
- **Spread scheduled jobs out.** Don't have every nightly job start on the hour
  against the same office; offset them.
- **Back off on failure** rather than retrying immediately — retry storms are what
  turn a blip into an outage.

**Why does this spec differ from the vendor's?**
It's additive: everything FieldRoutes documents is here, plus endpoints and fields
that are real and in use but undocumented upstream, plus corrections where the
vendor's docs are wrong. See the caveat below.

**Something looks wrong here.**
[Open an issue](https://github.com/alecbolingbroke/docs/issues) with
the endpoint and what you observed. For account, key, or platform issues, go to
**apisupport@fieldroutes.com** instead.

_Doc caveats: the vendor's own docs mislabel some fields (e.g. `group.date` is last-updated, not a service date) and mark some as required that aren't. This spec corrects them._
